I need to work out the spiral pattern for 18x18 by tracing through the 8x8 example row by row, checking where each ring's border stops one short as the spiral winds inward.

This confirms the general pattern: each layer's arm walks along one row/column but stops one short of the previous boundary, so the spiral inset shrinks by roughly one on each pass — right along a row, down a column, left along a row, up a column, then repeating inward with the same shrinking rule.

Continuing the arm-by-arm bound update, I verify the pattern holds for row4 with left-arm and right-arm contributions matching, confirming each ring layer leaves a one-cell gap from the previous. Now I'm setting up to simulate the full 18x18 grid ring by ring with these boundary rules.

Simulating ring bounds...

Continuing the spiral inward until the arms collapse, I reach the center and confirm it matches the expected 8x8 pattern, so I'm ready to build out the full 18x18 grid following this same spiral rule.

Mapping out row by row now...

Continuing the pattern down through rows 12-17, verifying against the smaller 8x8 analog to confirm the border and diagonal-fill structure, then starting to translate these row patterns into actual array values for each row.

Still mapping out maze grid rows...

I need to work out the spiral pattern by tracing through a smaller 8x8 example first, checking how the border traces around and where the gaps appear before scaling the logic up to 19x19.

Continuing this shrinking-spiral pattern, I keep tracking the boundary offsets—each row/col segment shrinks by 2 as I spiral inward, alternating between rows and columns until I nearly reach the center, where I need to double-check whether the last move goes up or down.

Checking the boundary case confirms it stops there. Now I'm laying out the full 19x19 grid by listing each spiral segment in order — the top row, right column, bottom row, left column, and so on, shrinking inward each time to trace the nested square pattern.

Continuing to trace through rows 5-10, filling in the active columns for each row based on where the spiral segments D through S pass through, building up the grid pattern row by row.

I finish tracing rows 11 through 18, closing out the spiral pattern where each nested segment (N, O, L, J, K, H, F, G, D, C, B) merges into the growing set of active columns, until row 18 has every column active. With row 1 confirmed to match the same pattern, I'm ready to construct the full grids.
